_what: The citation ledger (design doc §4.2 row 32): every #src-N entry, in order. cite:true marks the entries the JSON-LD 'citation' array mirrors. intro_tail and note_lead are this page's own sentences inside the constant framing (the source-class sentence, the dating policy and the re-check cadence stay in the partial). pre/post are layout-fidelity fields that keep the rebuilt v41 byte-identical: v41 appended entries 8–11 on one line, so 8 carries pre 8 spaces + post empty and 9–11 carry both empty. A new page omits them (the defaults are one entry per line).
intro_tail: Sources 1 to 4 are individual HVAC companies describing their own service calls in their own markets, not national research.
note_lead: The air filter price is a retail part cost, not a repair, and carries no citation because no source we would stand behind publishes a national figure for it.

list.note: Travis Baugh; expert review by Michelle Notaro, Product Manager for Residential Air Conditioners at Carrier Corporation. The figure appears in the page’s FAQ. No publication or update date is displayed. Verified Sept. 1, 2026. Supports the $200 to $1,500 published repair range.

list.title: Will Frozen AC Fix Itself? A Guide to Frozen AC Coils
list.note: Ryan Mayes; expert review by Michelle Notaro, Product Manager, Air Conditioners. No publication or review date is displayed; the site carries a general copyright line only. Verified Sept. 1, 2026. Supports switching cooling off immediately with the fan left running, and the compressor damage warning.

list.title: Help! My AC Evaporator Coil Is Frozen
list.note: No publication date is displayed. Trane also warns not to chip away at the ice, which can damage the coil. Verified Sept. 1, 2026. Supports switching the thermostat from COOL to OFF, and the major-damage warning.

list.title: Understanding AC Capacitors: A Comprehensive Guide
list.note: Travis Baugh; expert review by Michelle Notaro. No publication date displayed. Carrier gives $100 to $400 covering part and professional installation; we publish the narrower $150 to $400 because Carrier’s own figure of $75 to $150 per hour for technician time makes the $100 floor an edge case. Verified Sept. 1, 2026. Supports the $150 to $400 capacitor replacement range.

list.title: How to Fix a Refrigerant Leak in Your AC Unit
list.note: Travis Baugh; no expert reviewer listed. The figure appears in the page FAQ and Carrier footnotes it to Angi. No publication date displayed. The range stays open ended because a leak in the evaporator coil can cost more than the top of it. Verified Sept. 1, 2026. Supports the $250 to $1,600+ leak repair range.

list.title: How Much Does It Cost to Clean AC Coils?
list.note: Staff writer, reviewed by HomeAdvisor editor Ryan Noonan. Page displays Updated Jun 20, 2026. A cost aggregator that also sells contractor leads, so treated as a market reference rather than an authority. The low end is a cleaning bundled into an annual tune up; the high end is an acid wash deep clean. Verified Sept. 1, 2026. Supports the $75 to $350 condenser coil cleaning range.

list.title: Air Conditioner Repair Cost
list.note: Alexis Carthan; expert review by Richard Trethewey. Updated 03/16/2026. A cost guide carrying an advertiser disclosure, with figures compiled from Angi and Home Depot estimates rather than first party data. A frozen coil caused by a dirty filter resolves at service call money; one caused by a damaged coil runs to the top of the range. Verified Sept. 1, 2026. Supports the $150 to $2,500 spread for a frozen evaporator coil, which depends entirely on the underlying cause.
